what_it_does: This paper addresses a practical problem for system administrators: when you want to buy hardware to run Ceph (an open-source distributed storage system), how much CPU, memory, and disk bandwidth do you actually need? The authors perform empirical testing by running Ceph on various hardware configurations and measuring how input/output (I/O) performance changes. They use Linux hotplug (dynamically adding or removing CPU cores) and Cgroups (resource containers that limit processor and memory resources) to systematically vary the hardware available to the storage system and characterize the resulting performance.
